label: History
value: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor.
unit: Adrian Treleaven traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor to recover from typhoid fever and to visit the ancestral home of his grandparents, John and Damaris Tremayne. While staying at Echo Cottage as a boarder with Lorna Vane, he discovered the handwritten life-book of Captain Saul Garrick and received permission to adapt the captain's maritime adventures into a novel. Over the course of the summer, Adrian worked on his book at the lighthouse and developed a deep, silent love for Lorna Vane, though he kept his feelings secret out of respect for her marriage. Before departing, he confided his love for Lorna to Nell Harcourt, believing he would never see Lorna again. Later, after it was discovered that Lorna's missing husband had died years prior and that she was legally free, Adrian returned to Seven Gulls, declared his love for her, and they became engaged. The two were married the following June in the garden of Echo Cottage.

label: History
value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley.
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby resides in Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, where she keeps a keen watch over all passersby. A prominent community figure, she directs the local Sewing Circle, assists with the Sunday school, and acts as a pillar of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Obed Abernethy unexpectedly leaves town, her curiosity drives her to visit Grey Shutters, where Thirza Abernethy reveals that they are taking in an orphan child, an act Mrs. Agatha strongly condemns as risky. Upon meeting the orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, Mrs. Agatha bluntly criticizes her freckles and red hair, provoking Nell into a furious outburst. Though initially shocked, she forgives Nell after receiving a dramatic apology. Over time, Mrs. Agatha grows fond of Nell and takes interest in her progress at school and her community activities, such as the Village Improvement Society. Later, after her long-invalid husband Thomas Sowerby passes away, Mrs. Agatha faces financial difficulties due to an old mortgage on their farm.

A prominent community figure, she directs the local Sewing Circle, assists with the Sunday school, and acts as a pillar of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Obed Abernethy unexpectedly leaves town, her curiosity drives her to visit Grey Shutters, where Thirza Abernethy reveals that they are taking in an orphan child, an act Mrs. Agatha strongly condemns as risky. Though initially shocked, she forgives Nell after receiving a dramatic apology. Over time, Mrs. Agatha grows fond of Nell and takes interest in her progress at school and her community activities, such as the Village Improvement Society. Later, after her long-invalid husband Thomas Sowerby passes away, Mrs. Agatha faces financial difficulties due to an old mortgage on their farm.

A prominent community figure, she directs the local Sewing Circle, assists with the Sunday school, and acts as a pillar of the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Obed Abernethy unexpectedly leaves town, her curiosity drives her to visit Grey Shutters, where Thirza Abernethy reveals that they are taking in an orphan child, an act Mrs. Agatha strongly condemns as risky. Upon meeting the orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, Mrs. Agatha bluntly criticizes her freckles and red hair, provoking Nell into a furious outburst. Though initially shocked, she forgives Nell after receiving a dramatic apology. Over time, Mrs. Agatha grows fond of Nell and takes interest in her progress at school and her community activities, such as the Village Improvement Society. Later, after her long-invalid husband Thomas Sowerby passes away, Mrs. Agatha faces financial difficulties due to an old mortgage on their farm.

label: History
value: During a heated political campaign fifteen years ago, Ambrose Kerr publicly vowed to refrain from cutting his hair.
unit: During a heated political campaign fifteen years ago, Ambrose Kerr publicly vowed to refrain from cutting his hair or shaving his beard until the Liberal (Grit) party returned to power in Canada. He strictly maintained this vow for a decade and a half, growing a long, wild beard and mane of hair. Following a Liberal victory, he forced a local barber out of bed after midnight to cut his hair and shave his beard, startling his housekeeper upon returning home smoothly shaven. He eventually married his longtime friend and sparring partner, Miss Winifred Tolley, and moved into her house. He frequented the Seven Gulls lighthouse, sharing stories, debates, and musical evenings with Captain Saul Garrick, Hugh Carrow, and Nell Harcourt.

label: History
value: Anthony Tulk moved to Brierley
unit: Anthony Tulk moved to Brierley to live with his aunt, Mrs. Laurence Tulk, and enrolled at the local school. Initially taught under Mr. Pidgeon, he later fell under the instruction of Nell Harcourt, whom he initially disdained because of her gender. On her first day, he glared at her and openly stated his dislike for female teachers. Months later, he poured slate water down a classmate's neck and put a mouse in Nell's desk drawer. After being punished with a hardwood pointer, his attitude shifted, and he began showing respect and helpfulness toward Nell. He later joined the advanced class preparing for the Entrance examination, though he expressed doubt about the value of higher education for orphans. After failing to pass his exams on the first attempt, he returned to Brierley school for a second year before eventually passing and leaving for the West.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia's father died at sea.
unit: Aunt Euphemia's father died at sea shortly before her birth, leading to her being named Jamesina, though she went by Euphemia. She grew up in a family with six daughters and later married, though her husband passed away, as did her only daughter's departure for missionary work in India. Left alone in a large house, she agreed to move to Portmaris to keep house for her niece Mabel Colby and her friends Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay at Tabby's Place. She quickly became a beloved, reassuring presence in their lives, accommodating their friends and pets, including three cats. She managed the household for two academic years, providing the young women with a home-like environment. When the girls graduated from Wexcombe College, she decided to remain at Tabby's Place to care for her cats and the house rather than travel.

label: History
value: Barney Pullen grew up in Brierley
unit: Barney Pullen grew up in Brierley as part of the Gorham Pullen family. During the Brierley Sunday-school picnic, he ferried attendees on the Lake of Glassy Waters and saved his sister Odette from drowning when she fell over. He later drove Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke to the Sunday-school concert. As he grew older, he developed a deep crush on Nell Harcourt. Lacking the courage to propose in person, he persuaded his sister Odette to propose to Nell on his behalf after his father gave him the upper farm. After Nell rejected the proposal, he pursued and married Nettie Scobie.

He later drove Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke to the Sunday-school concert. As he grew older, he developed a deep crush on Nell Harcourt. Lacking the courage to propose in person, he persuaded his sister Odette to propose to Nell on his behalf after his father gave him the upper farm. After Nell rejected the proposal, he pursued and married Nettie Scobie.

label: History
value: Belinda was hired at age fourteen.
unit: Belinda was hired at age fourteen to serve as the housemaid for Miss Rosalind Penrose at Echo Cottage, taking the place of her older sisters who had previously held the same role. She quickly developed an intense devotion to Miss Rosalind and adapted enthusiastically to the imaginative life at Echo Cottage, forming a warm friendship with Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. She assisted during the famous night when Nell and Isolde accidentally jumped onto old Miss Lavinia Pembroke's bed in the dark. Later, Belinda tried to defend Miss Rosalind's reputation when old Miss Lavinia was furious, admitting that the jump was Nell's idea. When Miss Rosalind reconciled with her former lover, Stephen Stanhope, Belinda loyally kept their secret and helped prepare for the wedding. Following Miss Rosalind's marriage to Mr. Stanhope, Belinda moved with them to Boston. She eventually married a bricklayer named Tom, though she continued her service to Miss Rosalind and visited St. Brendan's Island during the summers.

label: Appearance
value: Captain Saul was a tall man.
unit: Captain Saul was a tall, stooped, and somewhat awkward man, though he retained an impression of immense physical power and endurance. He had an iron-gray, thick mane of hair that hung down to his shoulders, a closely shaved, bronzed, and heavily furrowed face, a rough mouth, and deep-set, exceptionally blue eyes that could twinkle, dream, or gaze wistfully at the sea. In his final months, he became noticeably frailer, paler, and more stooped.

label: History
value: Saul Garrick was born in Seven Gulls.
unit: Born in Seven Gulls, Saul Garrick felt an early, irresistible urge to go to sea. In his youth, he formed a deep friendship with the schoolmaster John Tremayne and fell in love with a girl named Margaret, whose tragic death at sea left him permanently devoted to her memory. For over fifty years, Captain Saul sailed the globe, surviving mutinies, shipwrecks, and pirate encounters, eventually retiring to become the keeper of the Seven Gulls Point lighthouse. Eleven years before his death, he discovered the amnesiac Laurence Vane in Havana and returned him to Seven Gulls, believing him to be Rufus Vane. In his later years, he became a beloved figure to Dr. Hugh Carrow and Nell Harcourt, welcoming them warmly into his life and lighthouse. He befriended young author Adrian Treleaven, allowing him to adapt his cherished 'life-book' into a novel. Shortly after receiving a published copy of his completed book, Captain Saul passed away peacefully at night in his lighthouse, resting his hands upon his life's story.

label: History
value: Clementine Ainslie grew up in an Episcopalian home.
unit: Clementine Ainslie grew up in an Episcopalian home on a hill overlooking Glen St. Agnes, suffering the early loss of her father and brother. At seventeen, she fell in love with young Martin Crawford, but he drowned at sea shortly thereafter. Following her mother's death when Clementine was twenty-five, she swore a solemn oath over the Bible to her grief-stricken sister Harriet that she would never marry and leave her alone. She lived quietly for years at the old family homestead, giving music lessons to local children. Later in life, she met the widowed Presbyterian minister John Ashdown at a forest spring. Although they fell in love, she initially refused his proposal of marriage due to her vow to Harriet. Eventually, Harriet released her from the oath upon deciding to marry her own former suitor, Lionel Fairlie. Clementine subsequently accepted Mr. Ashdown, winning the devotion of his four motherless children.

Following her rejection, he eventually recovered and married a sweet young woman with whom he found complete happiness.

label: History
value: Edmund grew up in Hollowmere.
unit: Edmund grew up in Hollowmere as the son of Dr. Hugh Carrow and Nell. He spent much of his childhood playing with his siblings and the manse children in Fern Hollow, where he frequently read poetry and shared imaginative stories with them. Although regarded by schoolmates as non-confrontational, he stood up to Dan Coyle when the latter insulted Grace Ashdown and his mother, successfully defeating Dan in a fight. Inspired by this victory over his fears, he subsequently agreed to go to the dentist to have a troublesome tooth extracted. As he grew older, he continued developing his talent for poetry, eventually earning praise for his written work.

label: History
value: Flossie attended Brierley school.
unit: Flossie attended Brierley school, where she frequently competed with Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow. She was caught peeking at her book during a spelling class by Nell, earning an icy look that made her blush. When Nell was punished by Mr. Pidgeon, Flossie grinned spitefully at her. She later participated in a game of 'daring' in the Pembroke garden, successfully walking the ridge of a wooden fence, and challenged Nell to walk the ridgepole of the kitchen roof, which led to Nell falling and spraining her ankle. Flossie was greatly relieved when Nell survived the fall. She joined the Regent's entrance class under Miss Thorne, though she disliked the bi-weekly recitation afternoons because she lacked creative imagination. She passed her entrance exams with a narrow three-point margin and attended Regent's Academy in Port Marlow. While at Regent's, she shared a boarding house with Frank Stockley and was known for her caustic tongue, though she remained on speaking terms with her classmates. She later took the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics during her Sophomore year at Wexcombe.

label: History
value: Grace grew up in Juneford.
unit: Grace grew up in Juneford as the second eldest child of the Reverend John Ashdown before moving with her family to the Glen St. Agnes manse. Lacking a mother's guidance, she and her siblings enjoyed an unrestrained upbringing, frequently engaging in lively escapades in Fern Hollow and the old Methodist cemetery. When rumors spread that their antics were bringing dishonor to their father, Grace joined her siblings in founding the Good-Conduct Club to discipline themselves. In an impulsive act of charity, she gave her only good black stockings to a barefoot girl, which eventually led to her attending church bare-legged and causing a local scandal. To clear her father of blame, she publicly addressed the congregation, and later confronted the formidable Lionel Fairlie, winning his respect and securing his financial support for her father's church. When her father eventually courted and married Clementine Ainslie, Grace warmly embraced her new stepmother, finding in her the guidance and affection her family needed.

label: History
value: Harriet Ainslie grew up at the old Ainslie house
unit: Harriet Ainslie grew up at the old Ainslie house on the hill overlooking Glen St. Agnes with her sister Clementine and her mother. In her youth, she was courted by Lionel Fairlie, but he deserted her after a quarrel and married another woman. Following the death of their mother when Clementine was twenty-five, Harriet was overcome with grief and fear of abandonment, extracting a solemn vow from Clementine that neither of them would ever marry. The sisters lived together quietly for decades. When the new minister, Mr. Ashdown, began visiting their home and eventually proposed to Clementine, Harriet fiercely insisted that Clementine abide by her oath. However, after Lionel Fairlie returned to court Harriet again and demanded her hand, Harriet realized her own desire for marriage and released Clementine from her vow. Harriet subsequently agreed to marry Lionel Fairlie.

label: History
value: Honora attended Regent's Academy.
unit: Honora attended Regent's Academy and studied alongside Nell Harcourt, excelling in languages and classical branches. After graduating, she taught school at Delford before enrolling at Wexcombe College. At Wexcombe, she formed a close circle of friends with Nell Harcourt, Mabel Colby, and Cressida Lindsay. Together with Nell, Mabel, and Cressy, she helped set up an independent household at 'Tabby's Place' in Portmaris. During her time at college, she achieved High Honors in Classics and formed lasting friendships before graduating with her Bachelor of Arts degree.

label: Quotes
value: > Nell, I’m terribly apologetic about mocking your hair. Truly I am. Please don’t stay angry forever.

label: Quotes
value: > I’m going to have my own way about my own house, I can tell you.

label: Quotes
value: > There is a dream I continue to hold, even if I have frequently felt it might never be realized. In this dream, there is a residence containing a burning hearth, a dog alongside a cat, the sound of friends approaching—and you!

value: > For a period back then, after you informed me that you could never care for me, Nell, nothing held much significance for me. label: Appearance
value: Hugh is a tall youth.
unit: Hugh is a tall, handsome youth with wavy chestnut hair, mischievous light-brown (hazel) eyes, and a broad-shouldered, athletic build. He has a firm, handsome chin and a lively, expressive face that often bears a mocking or friendly grin. Following a severe bout of typhoid fever, he appeared pale and thin for a time, but he retains a tall, manly posture as he matures into adulthood.

value: Hugh is lively.
unit: Hugh is lively, mischievous, and confident, with a keen sense of humor and a competitive drive. Though prone to teasing and occasional daring pranks in his early school days, he is deeply honorable, brave, and generous at heart, willing to admit his mistakes and make sacrifices for others. As he grows, he demonstrates a serious, dedicated work ethic toward his studies and medical vocation, maintaining high ideals while remaining warm, cheerful, and steadfastly loyal in his affections.

label: History
value: Hugh Carrow grows up in Brierley
unit: Hugh Carrow grows up in Brierley and spends three years of his childhood in Alberta with his father. Returning to Brierley School at fourteen, he initially teases Nell Harcourt by calling her 'Carrots', prompting her to break a slate over his head, an incident for which he immediately apologizes. Though Nell holds a grudge, Hugh competes with her academically at school and later at Regent's Academy. After working as a teacher at Pale Sands and a journalist at the Daily News to fund his education, he attends Wexcombe College, where he becomes captain of the Freshman football team, joins the Lambda Theta fraternity, and earns High Honors in Classics alongside the Cooper Prize. Upon learning Nell wishes to teach in Brierley to stay near her foster-mother, Hugh unselfishly withdraws his own application for the Brierley school so she can have it, taking the Pale Sands position instead. Over time, his early romantic overtures are rejected by Nell, leading to a period of distant friendship while rumor links him to Rowena Calder. However, after surviving a near-fatal bout of typhoid fever and completing his medical degree, Hugh's steadfast love for Nell is finally reciprocated. Upon taking over his great-uncle Dr. David Carrow's practice in Seven Gulls, Hugh leases a small white house by the harbour shore. He and Nell are married in the apple orchard at Grey Shutters and settle in Seven Gulls, where they later welcome their son, James Obed (Little Kit).

label: History
value: Ida resides at the Glen St. Agnes manse
unit: Ida resides at the Glen St. Agnes manse as the daughter of the local Presbyterian minister. After her mother's death, she and her siblings grew up with little supervision, forming a close bond with each other and the Carrow children, frequently playing in Fern Hollow and the local cemetery. When a runaway orphan named Mary Stubbs arrived, Ida showed her great compassion, sharing her bed and advocating for her to be allowed to stay. Ida participated in founding the Good-Conduct Club with her siblings to discipline themselves and spare their father embarrassment. Following a misdeed, she participated in a day-long fast as self-punishment and fainted during a church service from exhaustion. Fearing that their bad behavior would prevent her father from remarrying and finding happiness, Ida bravely visited Clementine Ainslie on her own, overcoming her fear of stepmothers to ask Clementine to marry her father. Her selfless plea moved Clementine, leading to the reconciliation and eventual marriage of her father and Clementine.

label: History
value: Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill near Brierley. At eleven years old, she became the bosom friend and confidante of Nell Harcourt, sealing their friendship with a solemn 'oath' over an imaginary stream in her garden. Together they created playhouses such as Larkrise, named local spots, and attended Brierley school together, where Isolde excelled academically and socially. Despite initial friction when her mother briefly forbade her from playing with Nell over a currant wine misunderstanding, Isolde remained devoted to her friend.

label: History
value: John Ashdown previously served as a minister at Juneford.
unit: John Ashdown previously served as a minister at Juneford, where his beloved wife, Cecilia, died shortly after giving birth to their youngest child, Ida. He was left a widower with four young children and the assistance of an elderly relative, Aunt Martha. He was called to Brierley and Glen St. Agnes to replace the retiring Mr. Bentley, where he won over the congregation with his engaging sermons, despite his impractical nature and absent-mindedness. For years, he remained consumed by grief for his late wife and struggled to manage his wild, motherless children. Eventually, he fell in love with Clementine Ainslie, an elegant parishioner from the hill. Although she initially rejected his proposal due to a secret oath made to her sister, her young stepdaughter-to-be, Ida, visited her and persuaded her to reconsider. Clementine accepted him, and their upcoming marriage brought immense joy and new order to his family.

label: History
value: Lionel Fairlie courted Harriet Ainslie in his youth.
unit: In his youth, Lionel Fairlie courted Harriet Ainslie, but following a disagreement he rashly married Dinah Coyle out of spite. His wife later passed away, leaving him a widower. After a dispute over a cow with a church elder, he stopped attending church services for twenty years. Years later, young Grace Ashdown confronted him at his farm to ask him to return to church and contribute to the minister's salary. Impressed by her fiery spirit when she berated him for his bluster, Lionel agreed to contribute generously and attend service once a month. His return to church reawakened his affection for Harriet Ainslie, whom he began pursuing openly. Harriet eventually agreed to release a past vow and accepted his proposal, leading to their planned autumn wedding.

unit: In his youth, Lionel Fairlie courted Harriet Ainslie, but following a disagreement he rashly married Dinah Coyle out of spite. His wife later passed away, leaving him a widower. After a dispute over a cow with a church elder, he stopped attending church services for twenty years. Years later, young Grace Ashdown confronted him at his farm to ask him to return to church and contribute to the minister's salary. Impressed by her fiery spirit when she berated him for his bluster, Lionel agreed to contribute generously and attend service once a month. His return to church reawakened his affection for Harriet Ainslie, whom he began pursuing openly. Harriet eventually agreed to release a past vow and accepted his proposal, leading to their planned autumn wedding.

label: Appearance
value: As a newborn, Little Kit weighed ten pounds.
unit: As a newborn, he weighed ten pounds, possessed lung power, and had soft fuzz on his head that was predicted to be red, though his father preferred to see it as hazel like his own. He has a forehead identical to his father's, and his small ears are perfectly shaped, sitting flat against his head. By his second year, he is described as a plump, chubby child with red, curly hair and hazel eyes that crinkle shut when he falls asleep.

label: History
value: Little Kit was born in Seven Gulls Harbor.
unit: Little Kit was born at the small house of dreams in Seven Gulls Harbor in the month of June. His birth brought immense healing and comfort to his mother, Nell, following the loss of her firstborn daughter the previous year. He was named James Obed Carrow after Captain Saul Garrick and Obed Abernethy. During his infancy, he was doted on by his family and neighbors, including Captain Saul, who bequeathed his collection of sea curiosities to him. As a young child, he remained closely cared for by his mother and Tabitha Pratt.

unit: Lorna possesses a deep, proud, and passionate nature that is fiercely loyal to her loved ones. The intense tragedies of her youth left her reserved, guarded, and occasionally prone to bitterness or quiet despair. Beneath her distant exterior, however, she has a rich capacity for joy, a vivid imagination, and a warmth that blossoms in the company of true friends.

label: History
value: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls.
unit: Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls, experiencing severe poverty and devastating family losses, including the accidental death of her brother Julian and her father's suicide. Highly ambitious, she completed two years of study in one at Regent's Academy to become a teacher, hoping to work her way through college. However, her mother coerced her into marrying Rufus Vane at age sixteen to save their farm from foreclosure. Rufus deserted her shortly after, but when Captain Saul brought back a brain-injured man from Havana, Lorna faithfully cared for him for eleven years, believing him to be Rufus. During this time, she befriended Nell Harcourt, though she initially struggled with secret envy over Nell's happy life. When Dr. Hugh Carrow suggested the man could be cured through surgery, Lorna bravely took him to Montreal, where the operation revealed the man was actually Rufus's cousin, Laurence Vane, and that Rufus had died years earlier in Cuba. Freed from her tragic bond, Lorna returned to Seven Gulls and fell in love with author Adrian Treleaven. They became engaged and planned to marry in the winter before moving to Japan.

label: History
value: After the death of Mary Farrow, Lucy was taken in by Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt to live at Grey Shutters.
unit: After the death of her mother, Mary Farrow, Lucy and her twin brother Robin were taken in by Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt to live at Grey Shutters. During her first winter there, she fell ill with croup, but her life was saved by Nell's prompt care before the doctor arrived. Lucy quickly settled into farm life, tending a tidy little garden plot and helping Thirza with light household tasks and chores. In contrast to her mischievous twin, she remained consistently polite and gentle, though Robin frequently coaxed or threatened her into minor misadventures, such as walking a pigpen fence or skipping Sunday School. As she grew into a teenager, she continued to attend the local school in Brierley and began taking music lessons from Clementine Ainslie. By the age of seventeen, she had attracted her first suitor, Ralph Pullen.

label: History
value: Mabel Colby worked as a rural schoolteacher.
unit: Mabel Colby worked for two years as a rural schoolteacher across nine grades, during which she grew weary of the trials of teaching and boarding in the country. She decided to pursue higher education at Wexcombe College, entering as a Sophomore due to her prior studies. Wanting to avoid boardinghouses, she proposed that she, Nell Harcourt, and Honora Hollis rent a house together in Portmaris, managed by her Aunt Euphemia. Joined by Cressida Lindsay, the group moved into Tabby's Place on Linden Avenue. Mabel participated in the girls' Story Club, writing creative tales, and successfully progressed through her studies at Wexcombe, ultimately graduating alongside her friends.

label: History
value: Mary fled from Mrs. Grimble
unit: Fleeing the severe cruelty of Mrs. Grimble, Mary ran away to Glen St. Agnes, where she hid in an old barn until discovered by the Ashdown children. Weak from starvation, she was brought to the manse, fed, and befriended by the minister's children, particularly forming a bond with Ida and Grace. Soon afterward, news arrived that Mrs. Grimble had died, leaving Mary free from her former bond. Fearing a return to the asylum or assignment to another harsh household, Mary found an advocate in Ida Ashdown, who pleaded her case to Miss Winifred (Mrs. Ambrose Kerr). Impressed by Mary's honesty and industrious nature, Mrs. Kerr took her in to live at her home, where Mary thrived under firm but compassionate care. Mary quickly adapted to her new life, taking pride in her domestic duties, joining the local school, and taking part in games in Fern Hollow alongside the Ashdown and Carrow children. Although she occasionally engaged in mischief—such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's collar in church or scaring children with ghost stories—she proved her loyalty by fiercely defending Mr.

Soon afterward, news arrived that Mrs. Grimble had died, leaving Mary free from her former bond. Fearing a return to the asylum or assignment to another harsh household, Mary found an advocate in Ida Ashdown, who pleaded her case to Miss Winifred (Mrs. Ambrose Kerr). Impressed by Mary's honesty and industrious nature, Mrs. Kerr took her in to live at her home, where Mary thrived under firm but compassionate care. Mary quickly adapted to her new life, taking pride in her domestic duties, joining the local school, and taking part in games in Fern Hollow alongside the Ashdown and Carrow children. Although she occasionally engaged in mischief—such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's collar in church or scaring children with ghost stories—she proved her loyalty by fiercely defending Mr.

value: Nell is a tall girl.

label: History
value: Nell arrives at Grey Shutters as an eleven-year-old orphan mistaken for a boy.
unit: Arriving at Grey Shutters as an eleven-year-old orphan mistaken for a boy, Nell quickly wins over the timid Obed Abernethy and stern Thirza Abernethy with her loquacious, imaginative spirit. She forms a deep friendship with her neighbor Isolde Pembroke, naming local landmarks such as Linger Lane, Reedmere, and the Nymph's Well. Attending Brierley school, she engages in a fiery academic rivalry with Hugh Carrow that evolves over time into a deep mutual affection. After a tragic mix-up involving an amethyst brooch and a missed picnic, she integrates fully into community life and Sunday-school. When Obed Abernethy dies of a heart attack following the failure of the Abbey Bank, Nell declines a university scholarship to stay in Brierley and teach school so Thirza will not have to sell Grey Shutters. She saves the life of young Posy Fay during a bout of croup and continues her own studies at home, eventually attending Regent's Academy, where she wins the prestigious Avery Scholarship. Rather than entering university immediately, she teaches for two years at Brierley School to earn her own way. She later attends Wexcombe College, living at 'Tabby's Place' with college friends and earning High Honors in English. After rejecting a proposal from Cyril Lisle, she realizes her true love is Hugh Carrow. Following her graduation, she marries Hugh in the orchard at Grey Shutters and moves to his new medical practice at Seven Gulls Harbor, living in their 'house of dreams.' There she gives birth to a daughter, Joy, who dies in infancy, but she later finds healing and joy in raising her son, Little Kit.

value: Obed Abernethy is extremely bashful.

Despite his extreme shyness, he possesses a soft, sympathetic heart and a quiet stubbornness once his mind is made up.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters in Brierley.
unit: He lived at Grey Shutters in Brierley with his sister Thirza, working his farm. Needing help due to advancing age, he agreed to adopt a young Canadian orphan boy. When he went to Alder River station, he discovered that a mistake had been made and an orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, was sent instead. Unable to leave her stranded, he brought her home and quietly advocated for keeping her. He developed a strong bond with Nell, frequently supporting her and purchasing gifts for her. After suffering from worsening heart trouble, he collapsed and died upon learning that the bank holding his life savings had failed. He was buried in the local Brierley cemetery, remembered with deep affection by his household.

label: History
value: Opal attends Brierley School.
unit: Opal attends Brierley School alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke, where she is known for her flirting and dramatic tendencies. She later attends Regent's Academy to prepare for her entrance exams, where she joins the Story Club and participates in the school concert. After graduating, she takes a teaching position in West Welby. During her first winter teaching, she contracts a severe lung illness that forces her to give up her job. As her health deteriorates over the following summer, she remains in denial about her condition, continuing to talk about her suitors and future plans. Eventually, she confesses her deep fear of dying and her longing to live to Nell. Before passing away, she reconciles with her former friend Em White and dies peacefully in her sleep.

label: History
value: Mr. J. A. Pettifer moved to Brierley
unit: Mr. J. A. Pettifer moved to Brierley from Scottsford, New Brunswick, buying the former Robert Bell farm next to Grey Shutters. His unusual housekeeping habits, lack of fixed mealtimes, and possession of a profane parrot named Nutmeg earned him a reputation as an eccentric crank. When a neighbor's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed into his oats, he confronted Nell Harcourt in a rage. Nell mistakenly sold his cow to a buyer, but she apologized and offered her own cow in trade, which led to the two becoming firm friends. Eventually, his estranged wife, Emily, tracked him down after reading a newspaper item and reunited with him, restoring immaculate order to his house. Though Nutmeg was killed during a severe thunderstorm, Mr. Pettifer remained content with his home life and continued as an active, supportive neighbor in the community.

His unusual housekeeping habits, lack of fixed mealtimes, and possession of a profane parrot named Nutmeg earned him a reputation as an eccentric crank. When a neighbor's Jersey cow repeatedly trespassed into his oats, he confronted Nell Harcourt in a rage. Nell mistakenly sold his cow to a buyer, but she apologized and offered her own cow in trade, which led to the two becoming firm friends. Eventually, his estranged wife, Emily, tracked him down after reading a newspaper item and reunited with him, restoring immaculate order to his house. Though Nutmeg was killed during a severe thunderstorm, Mr. Pettifer remained content with his home life and continued as an active, supportive neighbor in the community.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school.
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley school. During his tenure, he spent much of his time giving extra help to older students preparing for entrance exams, particularly Sukey Pullen, with whom he engaged in flirtatious behavior. His neglect of other students, poor discipline, and unfair punishments drew criticism from locals and students alike. On one occasion, he made Nell Harcourt stand on the dais for breaking her slate over Hugh Carrow's head after Hugh teased her about her hair. On another day, he punished Nell for arriving late by making her sit next to Hugh Carrow. At the Debating Club concert, he delivered an emotional recitation of Mark Antony's address over Caesar while looking at Sukey Pullen. At the end of the school year, he gave a moving farewell speech to his students before departing Brierley school.

label: History
value: Robin was born in Nova Scotia.
unit: Robin was born in Nova Scotia to a family with three sets of twins. After his father died, his mother dissolved the household, and his mother eventually fell ill and passed away. Following her death, Thirza Abernethy brought Robin and his twin sister Lucy to live at Grey Shutters in Brierley. At Grey Shutters, Robin quickly gained a reputation for being full of endless energy, curiosity, and mischief. Over the years, he got into numerous small scrapes, such as locking his sister in a toolhouse, dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, and putting a toad under Thirza's pillow. Despite these incidents, he formed a deep bond with Nell Harcourt and Thirza, growing steadily under their care into a healthy schoolboy. After his uncle passed away and left a small trust fund for the twins, Thirza formally decided to keep them permanently.

value: Rosalind Penrose grew up at Echo Cottage.
unit: Rosalind Penrose grew up at Echo Cottage, a secluded stone house in Middle Welby. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Stanhope, but her pride and a silly argument caused them to part ways, after which Stephen moved to the United States and she remained single. She lived a quiet, imaginative life at Echo Cottage alongside a series of young hired girls whom she collectively called Belinda. When Nell Harcourt visited her after a bed-jumping incident, Rosalind formed a warm bond with her and later welcomed Stephen's young son, Cedric, into her heart. Encouraged by Nell, Stephen visited Echo Cottage years after his first wife's death, leading to a reconciliation. Rosalind married Stephen in her garden beneath the honeysuckle trellis and subsequently moved to Boston, returning periodically to spend summers at Echo Cottage.

label: History
value: Rufus Vane operated a small sawmill.
unit: Rufus Vane operated a small sawmill up river and married Mrs. Rudge, with whom he had eight children, including three consecutive sets of twins. After his death, his household was dissolved. In Seven Gulls, he worked as a clerk in his father's store during the winter and sailed during the summer. Restless and persistent, he pursued Lorna Ainslie and forced her into marriage by threatening to foreclose on her widowed mother's farm mortgage. Shortly after her mother died, Rufus grew tired of domestic life and sailed for Havana aboard the Four Sisters alongside his cousin Laurence Vane. Rufus contracted yellow fever and died in Cuba thirteen years before the truth was revealed. Because Laurence suffered head trauma and amnesia in Havana, Captain Saul Garrick mistakenly brought Laurence back to Seven Gulls, where Lorna and the community believed the brain-damaged cousin was Rufus for eleven years until an operation in Montreal restored Laurence's memory.

label: History
value: Rupert relocated to Glen St. Agnes
unit: Rupert relocated to Glen St. Agnes with his father, brothers, and sisters, settling at the manse. He spent much of his free time playing in Fern Hollow and the old Methodist graveyard with his siblings and the Carrow children, frequently bringing caught insects, frogs, or garter snakes into the house. After Mary Stubbs arrived at the manse, Rupert participated in various outdoor pranks, such as leaping off the henhouse roof into straw and playing in the cemetery. During one trick, he tossed an allegedly dead eel into old Mrs. Carr's buggy, scaring her into jumping out and leading his father to attempt to discipline him with a switch, though his father ultimately could not bring himself to strike Rupert. Following the incident, Rupert accepted a self-imposed Club penalty of sitting on Hezekiah Pollock's tombstone until midnight in a cold rain, which caused him to contract a severe case of double pneumonia that nearly cost him his life before he recovered.

unit: Rupert relocated to Glen St. Agnes with his father, brothers, and sisters, settling at the manse. He spent much of his free time playing in Fern Hollow and the old Methodist graveyard with his siblings and the Carrow children, frequently bringing caught insects, frogs, or garter snakes into the house. After Mary Stubbs arrived at the manse, Rupert participated in various outdoor pranks, such as leaping off the henhouse roof into straw and playing in the cemetery. During one trick, he tossed an allegedly dead eel into old Mrs. Carr's buggy, scaring her into jumping out and leading his father to attempt to discipline him with a switch, though his father ultimately could not bring himself to strike Rupert. Following the incident, Rupert accepted a self-imposed Club penalty of sitting on Hezekiah Pollock's tombstone until midnight in a cold rain, which caused him to contract a severe case of double pneumonia that nearly cost him his life before he recovered.

value: Tabitha is a lean woman.

Her face is described as unlovely, and she has a distinct, sharp manner.

value: Tabitha is a fiercely loyal woman.
unit: Tabitha is a fiercely loyal, practical, and hardworking woman who takes immense pride in her domestic duties, particularly her cooking and baking. Though she can be sharp-tongued, austere, and critical of others—especially men, whom she often views with suspicion—she possesses a deep, maternal affection for those in her care. She is fiercely protective of children, deeply devoted to Mrs. Doctor Carrow and her family, and holds firm, opinionated views on proper conduct and household management.

label: History
value: Tessa Carrow is born at Hollowmere
unit: Tessa Carrow is born at Hollowmere, Glen St. Agnes, as the youngest child of Nell Harcourt and Dr. Hugh Carrow. She spends three months in Brierley with her siblings while her parents travel in Europe, returning to Hollowmere in the spring. One afternoon, Tabitha sends her to the manse to deliver a basket of early strawberries directly to Mr. Ashdown or Aunt Martha. At the manse gate, Mary Stubbs corners her, trying to seize the basket, and performs a wild, intimidating dance to scare her. When Tessa refuses to hand over the basket, Mary chases her down the street waving a large dried codfish. Terrified, Tessa trips into a mud puddle, ruining her fine dress, hat, and slippers, and spilling the strawberries. Miss Winifred rescues the crying girl and carries her back to Hollowmere, where Tabitha cleans and comforts her.

label: History
value: Thirza resides at Grey Shutters
unit: Thirza resides at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her quiet brother, Obed Abernethy. Expecting to take in an orphan boy to help on the farm, she is shocked when Obed brings home a fiery, red-haired eleven-year-old orphan girl named Nell Harcourt instead. Though initially determined to send Nell back, Thirza relents out of compassion for the girl's past and at Obed's quiet insistence. Over the years, Thirza works diligently to train the imaginative Nell in practical household skills, proper morality, and religion, gradually forming a fierce, motherly love for her. When Obed dies suddenly following the failure of the Abbey Bank, Thirza faces the prospect of losing Grey Shutters, but Nell decides to forego her college scholarship to teach locally and keep the farm. Eventually, after facing impending blindness that limits her labor, Thirza agrees to let Mrs. Agatha Sowerby move into Grey Shutters, allowing Nell to finally attend Wexcombe College. Thirza later takes in two orphan twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow. She experiences intense pride as Nell succeeds academically, wins the Avery Scholarship, and marries Dr. Hugh Carrow, the son of her own youthful suitor.

label: History
value: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the Brierley school trustees.
unit: Miss Agnes Thorne was hired by the Brierley school trustees to serve as the village's first female schoolteacher. In the autumn following her arrival, she established alternating Friday afternoon recitation programs, biweekly nature field days, and daily physical culture exercises for her pupils. She formed a special late-afternoon class for proficient students preparing for the Regent's Academy entrance examination. Although she considered accepting a position in her home district's grade school at the end of her first year, she chose to return to Brierley to guide her students through their entrance exams. Under her instruction, her entrance class achieved notable success, including a tied top score on the Island's entrance examination. At the conclusion of her second year, she departed from Brierley school.

label: History
value: Winifred Tolley spent her whole life as a spinster.
unit: Miss Winifred Tolley spent her whole life as a spinster residing at Seven Gulls. Known for her sharp-tongued independence and dislike of men, she nevertheless dedicated herself to acts of community charity, such as sewing clothes for needy children. When Nell Harcourt moved to Seven Gulls, Miss Winifred quickly became a close, supportive friend and frequent visitor to the house of dreams. Over time, she actively supported Lorna Vane, providing her with guidance and taking in a former orphan, Mary Stubbs, to live with her. In her late fifties, after years of declaring she would never marry, she surprised the community by accepting the marriage proposal of her long-time suitor, Ambrose Kerr, and moving him into her home.
